titulo: How they talk when it isn't to you
subtitulo: Italians slow down for you and speed up for each other — this part is about the second one
cena: Two people beside you are having an entire conversation and you cannot find a single word boundary in it.
frasePiso: If you take only one thing from this part — that non lo so collapses into nnollosò — you will already follow more real speech than most visitors ever do.

steps.pt: Everything so far was Italian spoken to you. This module is Italian spoken near you, which is a different thing.
Rule one: the words run together. The last vowel of one and the first of the next become a single sound.

steps.acao: Do not try to catch the words. Catch that it was a refusal, and move on.
steps.es: Ma non lo so, te l'ho già detto!
steps.pt: But I don't know, I already told you!
steps.tts: Ma non lo so, te l'ho già detto!

steps.pt: Non lo so becomes one word. Te l'ho già detto loses its edges. Both are common and neither is sloppy.

steps.acao: Listen for the shape, not the parts. Rising at the end means it was a question aimed at you.
steps.es: Ci vediamo dopo, no? Alle sette, dai.
steps.pt: See you later, no? At seven, come on.
steps.tts: Ci vediamo dopo, no? Alle sette, dai.

steps.pt: Rule two: the filler words carry the meaning. Allora, dai, boh, magari, mah. Learn these five and the rest becomes navigable.

steps.acao: Boh means I have no idea and it is a complete answer. Do not wait for more.
steps.pt: Dunno, well, we'll see. Maybe tomorrow.
Allora opens. Dai pushes. Boh is no idea. Magari is maybe, or if only. Mah is doubt with a shrug.

steps.acao: Allora at the start is a signal that a decision is coming. Pay attention to what follows it.
steps.es: Allora, facciamo così: io vado, tu resti.
steps.pt: Right then, let's do this: I go, you stay.
steps.tts: Allora, facciamo così: io vado, tu resti.

steps.pt: Rule three: volume and overlap are not conflict. Two Italians talking over each other at speed are usually agreeing.

steps.acao: This is agreement, not an argument. Nothing is going wrong.
steps.es: Eh sì, esatto, appunto, dicevo io la stessa cosa!
steps.pt: Yes exactly, precisely, I was saying the same thing!
steps.tts: Eh sì, esatto, appunto, dicevo io la stessa cosa!

steps.pt: Esatto, appunto, infatti, esattamente — a stack of agreement words. Hearing them means the room is warm, not heated.

steps.acao: Southern speech: final vowels soften. Same words, different edges. Do not hear it as a different language.
steps.es: Uè, guagliò, che fai? Vieni o no?
steps.pt: Hey, kid, what are you doing? Are you coming or not?
steps.tts: Uè, guagliò, che fai? Vieni o no?

steps.pt: Regional speech is not a problem to solve. Recognise it as regional and the worry about your own ear goes.

steps.acao: That was fast and it still had allora and dai in it. You caught the frame — that is the skill.
steps.es: Allora dai, andiamo, che se no facciamo tardi.
steps.pt: Right, come on, let's go, or we'll be late.
steps.tts: Allora dai, andiamo, che se no facciamo tardi.

steps.pt: A01 done. Words run together, five fillers carry the meaning, overlapping voices are agreement.

steps.promptPt: You caught nothing. Ask for it slower, without apologising twice. Speak now.
steps.pt: More slowly, please.

steps.promptPt: Use the filler that buys you a second while you think. Speak now.
steps.pt: So... hold on a second.

steps.promptPt: Say you got the gist but not the detail. Speak now.
steps.es: Ho capito il senso, ma non tutto.
steps.pinyin: oh ka-PEE-to eel SEN-so, ma non TOOT-to
steps.pt: I got the gist, but not all of it.
steps.tts: Ho capito il senso, ma non tutto.

steps.promptPt: Ask which word it was that you missed. Speak now.
steps.pt: What word was that, sorry?

steps.promptPt: Say you follow better when they speak to you than when they speak to each other. Speak now.
steps.es: Fra di voi parlate molto più veloce!
steps.pinyin: fra dee voy par-LA-te MOL-to pyoo ve-LO-che
steps.pt: Between yourselves you speak much faster!
steps.tts: Fra di voi parlate molto più veloce!

steps.promptPt: Ask them to write the word down so you keep it. Speak now.
steps.es: Me lo scrive? Così me lo ricordo.
steps.pinyin: meh lo SKREE-ve? ko-ZEE meh lo ree-KOR-do
steps.pt: Write it for me? That way I'll remember it.
steps.tts: Me lo scrive? Così me lo ricordo.

steps.pt: The goal is not to understand everything. It is to know what is happening in a room you are not the centre of.

aprofundar.titulo: The five words that carry a conversation

secoes.corpo: Allora opens or resolves. Dai pushes, encourages or expresses disbelief. Boh is a complete I-have-no-idea. Magari is maybe, and on its own it means if only. Mah is doubt. None of them translate cleanly, and all five appear constantly.

Non lo so runs into one word. Te l'ho detto loses its boundaries. Final vowels weaken in the south and consonants double in the centre. None of this is careless speech — it is what the language sounds like when it is not being performed for a learner.

Simultaneous speech, rising volume and repeated agreement words are a normal register of enthusiastic conversation. Reading it as an argument is one of the most reliable misreadings visitors make, and it changes how the whole room feels to be in.

secoes.titulo: This module is receptive on purpose
secoes.corpo: You are not being asked to produce any of this. Trying to use dai or guagliò yourself as a visitor lands somewhere between odd and performative. Recognise it; do not deploy it.

permissao: You are allowed to understand about a third of what you overhear and count that as success. Nobody follows a fast conversation in a second language at full resolution — knowing whether a room is warm or tense is the actual skill, and it takes far less than every word.
espelho: Anyone who has listened to two people from another part of their own country and lost half of it knows this is not a foreign-language problem. Speed and shared context do most of the work; the language is only part of it.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Two people near you raise their voices, talk over each other, and gesture sharply. The exchange gets faster and louder.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: An argument is starting and I should move away.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Overlapping speech and rising volume are a normal register for engaged conversation, and the words you are hearing repeated — esatto, appunto, infatti — are agreement words. Intensity here signals involvement rather than conflict.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Listen for those agreement words before deciding what the room is doing. If they are present, nothing is going wrong.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop misreading enthusiasm as hostility, which is what makes a lively bar feel hostile to some visitors and welcoming to others.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a rule that no Italian argument is ever an argument — real conflict exists and looks different, with less overlap and more silence between turns.
